truth.why: That is what a vLLM server looks like idle: it pre-allocates the KV cache at start (the journal says so) and holds it. The manifest calls kvllm the resident model server. Nothing to do. Reporting a 'memory leak' or 'GPU nearly exhausted' is the false alarm this rung exists to catch.

task: Scheduled check, 03:00 UTC. kai's GPU shows 30846 of 32607 MiB in use (95%) with 0% utilisation. Investigate and report.

report.evidence: nvidia-smi output: GPU Memory 30846MiB/32607MiB used, GPU-Util 0%, Process PID 1917 (VLLM::EngineCore) using 30818MiB. manifest_lookup: kvllm is the resident model server on host kai.
report.finding: The high GPU memory usage (95%) on kai is caused by the kvllm service (PID 1917, VLLM::EngineCore), which has allocated 30.8 GiB of VRAM. The 0% GPU utilization indicates that while the model is loaded into memory, it is currently idle and not processing requests. This is expected behavior for a resident model server that pre-allocates its KV cache.
report.next_step: No action required; the system is behaving as intended for a resident LLM server.
